clue.text: Clan's tartan — it's different from America?

indicators.note: different says the letters of the clan's tartan and 'it' are made into something other than they were

parts.note: read as 'it is': IT goes into the mix and the 'is' is a link

explanation.surface: A clan's tartan is claimed to look quite unlike anything from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'different': CLANSTARTANIT rearranged gives the answer. The question mark marks the definition as playful: to a Briton, something from America comes from across the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, anything American comes from the far side of the Atlantic Ocean, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Class write using keyboard

explanation.surface: A lesson in typing.
explanation.definitionFit: Type means both a category and to key in text on a keyboard.

clue.text: Authorise program range

parts.note: an app is a computer program, short for application
to range is to wander, to rove

explanation.surface: Permission is given for a range of software.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve is to sanction or officially authorise.

clue.text: Inform about time for swindle

indicators.note: about says the word for inform wraps around the abbreviation for time

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone tells the police about the timing of a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is slang for a confidence trick or swindle.

clue.text: Starts to talk up river — bags of tasty fish!

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An angler talks up a river and its catch of delicious fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: Shortened form of two books about getting into flying industry

indicators.note: getting into says the books and 'about' go inside the industry word

parts.note: aviation is the industry of flying aircraft
B is short for book, so two books give two Bs
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A short version of two books on breaking into the airline business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' places BBRE after the first letter of AVIATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation is a shortened version of a word or phrase.

clue.text: Headdress seen in trip abroad oddly

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions of the phrase trip abroad

explanation.surface: A jewelled headpiece is spotted on a foreign holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental crown worn on the head.

clue.text: Fine once to cry madly for sweets?

indicators.note: madly says the letters of the preceding words are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A child who was fine a moment ago now cries frantically for sugary treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' is the anagram signal for FINEONCETOCRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery is the collective term for sugary treats such as candy and chocolate.

clue.text: More lively PE initially performed by seaside feature

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of performed

parts.note: a pier is a structure typical of British seaside resorts

explanation.surface: A school gym lesson is held next to some feature of the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppier is the comparative of peppy, meaning full of energy and spirit.

clue.text: Bachelor artist, fashionable — bright guy

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: An unmarried, stylish painter is described as clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain is informally a very clever person, an intellectual.

clue.text: Left in Congo with this writer, assess business organisation

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for left sits inside the country name

parts.note: the African country, taken as written
the setter referring to themselves gives ME
to rate is to assess or evaluate

explanation.surface: Someone who departed and lives in the Congo evaluates a corporate body.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomerate is a large corporation formed by merging diverse companies.

clue.text: Be heedful in the race, Kate, when climbing

indicators.note: when climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words the race, Kate, across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone warns Kate to be cautious while ascending during the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unassigned; it is the hiding signal. In a down clue 'climbing' means read upwards, so the letters in 'thE RACE KATe' are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To take care is to be cautious and attentive, which is what heedful means.

clue.text: A part of poem, hostile

parts.note: a verse is a stanza, one section of a poem

explanation.surface: A stanza is antagonistic in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or strongly disinclined, a near synonym of hostile.

clue.text: Opening course for Aintree official?

definitions.meaning: the first course of a meal
Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National

explanation.surface: A first dish served to the man who starts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Starter means both an appetiser and the official who begins a race.

clue.text: Harsh to exclude northern girl

indicators.note: to exclude says one letter is left out of the harsh word

parts.note: violent means harsh or brutal

explanation.surface: A severe rule keeps out a young woman from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude' removes the N from VIOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Exotic eagle in descent

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare foreign eagle comes swooping down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage means ancestry, line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Unconvincing feel about opening of bowling, English

indicators.note: about says the word feel goes around the letter taken from bowling

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: opening of asks for just the first letter of bowling

explanation.surface: An English cricketer's feel for the start of his bowling is weak.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeble excuse or argument is weak and fails to persuade.

clue.text: In from France, learner entering cave area unlike its surroundings

parts.note: en is the French word for in

indicators.note: entering says the learner's letter goes into the word cave

parts.note: taken as written
L for learner, from the L-plates on learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: A trainee from France ventures into a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory or group entirely enclosed by a different, surrounding one.

clue.text: Husband in holiday area — a winner

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for husband sits inside the holiday area

parts.note: a camp is a place where holidaymakers stay
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A husband at a holiday site proves victorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is informal for champion, one who wins.

clue.text: Dance from Manhattan, good

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words that follow, across the word break

explanation.surface: A dance that comes out of New York is praised as good.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a Latin American ballroom dance originating in Argentina.

clue.text: Modify a dwelling on return at end of August

indicators.note: on return says the word for a dwelling is read backwards

parts.note: pad is slang for a home or flat

indicators.note: at end of picks only the final letter of August

explanation.surface: Someone alters their home after coming back at the close of August.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter it to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Ordered to include legendary bird in rich fabric

indicators.note: to include says the bird's name is placed inside the word for ordered

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is commanded to be woven into luxurious cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like an anagram signal but is BADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a heavy woven textile with a raised pattern, often in gold or silver thread.

clue.text: International trader, former doorman

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a porter guards the door of a building

explanation.surface: A one-time hotel doorman now deals in goods across borders.
explanation.definitionFit: An exporter sells goods to buyers in other countries.

clue.text: Extremely docile, weepy, moist

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters, of each word

explanation.surface: Someone very gentle and tearful has damp eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means wet with dew, hence slightly damp.
